author: smimon
text:
It's always worth checking LTF to see what our H1/H4 FTR/FL - that we "think" might have been engulfed - was formed as a reaction to.

Consider this flag that was formed a couple of weeks ago, as EJ made it's initial rise. This is M5:

Now look at the H1 picture:

The key to this up move (which I admittedly over-analysed and talked myself out of) was the engulf of the H1 FTR that formed after taking out a monthly level to the left. This was the most significant level in the local area, so when it was taken north, it was a sign we were destined to go higher at some point.

author: Rdk123
text:
I get the feeling that's the intention!

I think that when we have the limit of a FLAG hitting off a FL we're going to get confusion. Although the blue circle area is the limit of the FLAG, by definition it cannot be a FL. It's just a demand/decision.

But then that's where the FL article could be misleading (Again could be intentional), because it references S/R or a Base before the FL, when you look, some of the examples are before the engulf of the S/R or base, so maybe these DBR's have engulfed the previous FL but we know we need a DBR to form our FL. Basically the article doesn't tell us to look for what's holding up these DBRs, I think that's the problem, but I think we'd all agree we're probably better off for having to figure that out ourselves.

That was a lot of writing to come to that simple conclusion, apologies!

I hope that's not just jargon!

Robbie
